name: CUDA grid-stride saxpy kernel against CPU AVX2 and multithreaded saxpy (The C++ Programmer's Mindset, ch. 14)
listed_description: Book technique: CUDA grid-stride saxpy kernel compared with single-threaded AVX2 and multithreaded CPU saxpy.
reason: Code is in the repo (Chapter-14/saxpy.cu, saxpy_mt.cpp with target_clones("avx2,default") and a 4-thread OpenMP loop, bench_saxpy.cu over 1<<12 to 1<<30 elements) but no numbers anywhere reachable: the comparison exists only as a log-log plot in the book, and the repo holds no results file or README table. Directional claim only (GPU time flat until the device saturates, then linear but lower than the CPU versions). The benchmark keeps thrust::device_vector data resident, so host-device transfer is excluded. GPU model (RTX 5070Ti) and CPU come only from the book lead.

name: CUDA shared-memory tiled matrix multiplication (The C++ Programmer's Mindset, ch. 14)
listed_description: Book technique: 16x16 shared-memory tiled CUDA matmul kernel benchmarked against cuBLAS sgemm.
reason: Code is in the repo (Chapter-14/matmul.cu, bench_matmul.cu with cublasSgemm at 64, 256, 1024 and 4096 cubed) but the technique does not beat its named baseline: per the book lead it is slower than cuBLAS (16.1 versus 12.7 microseconds at 256, about 35 ms versus just over 4 ms at 4096), and the repo has no naive-kernel baseline. The only faster-than claim is a prose cross-comparison with the chapter-4 CPU GEMM numbers, which are a different size (1000x1000), precision (double) and run, so it is not a valid same-task measurement. No results file in the repo.

name: Hash function comparison: std::hash vs absl::Hash vs boost::hash (The C++ Programmer's Mindset, ch. 5)
listed_description: Book technique: Google Benchmark of std::hash, absl::Hash and boost::hash on int64, double and a 60-character string.
reason: Code is in the repo (Chapter-05/benchmark_hash.cpp, with an empty-loop baseline per type) but the claim is directional only: on GCC integers are comparable and std::hash is 'notably slower' for doubles and strings, with no numbers in the lead or in the repo (no results file, no README table). CMakeLists.txt sets no build type, flags or compiler.

name: QThreadPool with QRunnable
listed_description: Qt thread pool that recycles worker threads to run QRunnable tasks, with max thread count, expiry timeout and auto-delete controls.
reason: No numeric comparison reachable. The book only prints an active thread count. qtbase tests/benchmarks/corelib/thread/qthreadpool/tst_bench_qthreadpool.cpp times only QThreadPool::start of a no-op QRunnable and activeThreadCount(), with no QThread or std::thread per task baseline and no results in the repo. src/corelib/thread/qthreadpool.cpp and the Qt docs say recycling avoids the cost of creating and destroying threads (directional claim, no numbers). Web searches found no QThreadPool-versus-thread-per-task timings: generic pool shootouts (ThreadTest, d36u9/async, taskpool) omit QThreadPool, and asynqro benchmarks qtconcurrent only. Repo: 3.1k stars, Qt license set (GPL/LGPL/commercial).

name: BDE (Bloomberg Development Environment)
listed_description: Mature C++ library suite listed with Boost, Folly, Abseil, Qt and EASTL as ready-made code that helps write quality software faster.
reason: No numeric comparison reachable. The README and a grep of the bdlma allocator headers (sequential, buffered sequential, multipool, concurrent pool, pool) show no benchmark numbers; bslstl_unorderedmap.h only mentions hash-map performance versus ordered maps without figures. benchmarks/allocators/README.md points to the WG21 papers N4468, P0089R0 and P0089R1 ('On Quantifying Memory-Allocation Strategies') and to the archived fork bloomberg/bde-allocator-benchmarks (archived 2020-05-06, holds the benchmark code, README without results); the numbers live in those papers, but open-std.org is blocked here (ENOTFOUND) and searches returned no figures. Revisit via the papers: they compare BDE-style monotonic and multipool allocators with the default new/delete allocator. Repo: Apache-2.0, 1.9k stars, last commit 2026-10-23.
